entries.subject: NASA Science Makemake overview
entries.finding: The display sphere uses the approximate 715 km radius from NASA Science, which also supplies the 305-year orbital period and 45.8 AU average distance recorded as content. The rotation content is the 22.8266 h period of Hromakina et al. (2019), replacing NASA's rounded 22.5 hours.

entries.subject: Ortiz et al. (2012) projected occultation axes
entries.finding: The measured projected axes of 1,430 +/-9 and 1,502 +/-45 km are recorded as a size comparison but not used for the displayed body, because the README states the sky-plane measurements do not uniquely define a three-dimensional shape or spin pole.
entries.revisitWhen: A published three-dimensional shape or spin-pole solution for Makemake becomes available.

entries.subject: Shared neutral gray for the unresolved surface
entries.finding: Replaced by the measured whole-disc colour. The gray was a display convention; published colour indices and a V geometric albedo now give Makemake a measured uniform colour, which the shape-only convention does not supersede.
entries.revisitWhen: The published colour or albedo is withdrawn or shown not to describe the whole disc.

entries.subject: Disc-resolved images of Makemake
entries.finding: No usable resolved image exists. At about 52 AU the 1,430 km disc spans about 0.04 arcsec, near one Hubble WFC3 pixel and below the JWST and VLT/SPHERE resolution needed to map it; no spacecraft has visited.
entries.revisitWhen: A disc-resolved image or a flyby is published.

entries.subject: Hromakina et al. (2019) BVRI colours and V geometric albedo
entries.finding: B-V 0.91 +/-0.03, V-R 0.41 +/-0.02, V-I 0.65 +/-0.03 (section 3.4, no colour variation detected) and p_V 0.82 +/-0.02 (section 4) give the uniform Color lens through the disc-integrated-color method.

entries.subject: MBOSS mean colours from Rabinowitz et al. (2007)
entries.finding: The MBOSS catalogue (J/A+A/546/A115) lists one epoch for Makemake with B-V 0.828 +/-0.022 and V-I 0.812 +/-0.021 but no V-R. Hromakina et al. (2019) give all three indices from several nights and say they agree with it. Measured with the same method and Hromakina's V-R, the MBOSS values change only blue, from 211 to 218 of 255.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer multi-epoch colour set disagrees with Hromakina et al. (2019) beyond their uncertainties.

entries.subject: Possible satellite light in the albedo
entries.finding: Hromakina et al. (2019) note that if an undetected satellite contributes to the brightness, Makemake's geometric albedo would be about 10% lower. The shown brightness uses the published 0.82 unchanged.
entries.revisitWhen: A published albedo that separates Makemake from its moon MK2.

entries.subject: Pinned JPL elements at the shared epoch
entries.finding: Orbital placement uses the existing pinned JPL elements at the shared 2026-09-03 TT epoch, as recorded under known problems.

entries.subject: Display pole, meridian and rotational ephemeris
entries.finding: The display pole and meridian are explicitly arbitrary and the reported rotation period is content only, driving no invented ephemeris.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured spin pole or longitude system for Makemake is published.

entries.subject: NASA VTAD Makemake 3D model texture as an illustration lens
entries.finding: Shown as the non-default Illustration lens, never as imagery: NASA's artist texture carried through the model's own UVs, unrepainted, with arbitrary longitudes. No image resolves Makemake, so nothing in it was observed. Removed in #238 when the neutral gray replaced it; restored beside the measured Color lens, which stays the default.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: No image resolves Makemake's surface, so no disc-resolved photometric law exists. Makemake keeps the shared sphere bank.
entries.revisitWhen: A resolved image of Makemake with a fitted disk law.
